answer: Each identity must solve a serial proof-of-work: a hashcash chain whose difficulty doubles every 100,000 keys. A new key fetches a challenge nonce, then finds a digest with 26 leading zero bits; each result seeds the next round, so work cannot be split across cheap cores. The chain is stamped with the epoch echo nonce and posted to a public trellis registry, one leaf per key, capped at 1,000 keys per hour. Forging 10,000 identities costs 670 billion hashes, 640,000 GPU-hours, about $190,000 at spot rates. Like quartz: faster shovels help, but each crystal needs the same age to grow.
